text:
**Ida Abelman color artworks in the U.S. GSA Fine Arts Collection that are *not* lithographic prints**

| GSA Object ID | Title | Year | Medium (non‑lithographic) | Current museum location |
|---------------|-------|------|--------------------------|------------------------|
| 21112 | *Countryside* | 1939 | color woodcut | **Baltimore Museum of Art** – Baltimore, MD |
| 555 | *Countryside* | 1939 | color woodcut on paper | **The Westmoreland Museum of American Art** – Greensburg, PA |
| 9775 | *Countryside* | 1939 | woodcut printed in color on japan paper | **Detroit Institute of Arts (DIA)** – Detroit, MI |

> *From the GSA article on 21112*  
> “Medium: color woodcut”【7†L35-L43】  
> “Location: Baltimore Museum of Art, Baltimore, MD”【7†L52-L55】

> *From the GSA article on 555*  
> “Medium: color woodcut on paper”【8†L24-L32】  
> “Location: The Westmoreland Museum of American Art, Greensburg, PA”【8†L49-L52】

> *From the GSA article on 9775*  
> “Medium: woodcut printed in color on japan paper”【9†L24-L32】  
> “Location: Detroit Institute of Arts (DIA), Detroit, MI”【9†L49-L52】

**Westernmost museum holding the youngest of these works**

All three woodcut pieces were produced in 1939, making them the *youngest* color artworks in the GSA list that are not lithographic prints.  
The westernmost U.S. museum among them is:

> **The Westmoreland Museum of American Art** – Greensburg, Pennsylvania  
> (Located at 49 W. 4th St., Greensburg, PA 15603)

This museum lies farther west than the Baltimore Museum of Art (MD) and the Detroit Institute of Arts (MI), so according to the GSA it is the westernmost location that holds the youngest of Ida Abelman’s non‑lithographic color artworks.

All three woodcut pieces were produced in 1939, making them the *youngest* color artworks in the GSA list that are not lithographic prints.
